items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: By that time in my mind I was already going to be a Jazz Messenger.

ctx.x: Let me ask, when you were let’s say 15 or 16, you are playing the saxophone, you had a supportive family environment as far as music. Did you have aspirations at that age to be a professional musician?
Right. Absolutely. By that time in my mind I was already going to be a Jazz Messenger.

items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: Joining Art Blakey, that was something that he really emphasized for us to do... I’m the saxophonist, piano, bass and Art... anyone that played with Art or who watched Art play can attest to that.

ctx.x: Thank you. I’m looking forward to your concert here. But I wanted to start off asking you a little bit about something that I’m guessing is important to you and that is your composing.

I’m getting more involved with composing, very much involved with it now as the years have gone on. Joining Art Blakey, that was something that he really emphasized for us to do, writing, and it is very important to find your own self and some sense of your individuality through your own writing, so that’s very important.
I saw a recent addition to your website and that you’re going to do a film score for something in Syracuse?
